models.title: CAPM security market line expected return
models.summary: Asset expected return as the risk-free rate plus beta times the market risk premium.

relationship.original_equation: E[Ri] = rf + βi,mkt · (market risk premium); e.g. 6.62% = 2.5% + 1.03 (4%)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Reverse Optimization, printed p. 218 (PDF p. 228), Exhibit 12
relationship.translation_notes: Decimal form (unit 1). MRP is the market risk premium E[Rm] − rf over the same horizon. Used in the PDF to impute reverse-optimized expected returns from market betas (global market premium 4%, rf 2.5%). Dimensional check: dimensionless throughout.

variables.definition: Risk-free rate over the horizon, in decimal form
variables.context: same market and horizon as ERi

variables.definition: Asset sensitivity to the market portfolio (same meaning as batch b02 beta record)
variables.context: same asset and market portfolio as ERi

variables.definition: Expected market return in excess of the risk-free rate, in decimal form
variables.context: same market portfolio and horizon as ERi

variables.definition: CAPM-implied expected return of asset i, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset, market, and horizon as inputs

assumptions: Single-period CAPM equilibrium: every asset priced by its market beta with one market portfolio and one risk-free rate.
Source application: market-capitalization weights proxy the market portfolio; rf 2.5% and MRP 4% in the worked exhibit.
limitations: Equilibrium pricing assumption; deviations are the subject of the Black–Litterman views step (deferred full mathematics).
The risk-premium-only form RPi = β·RPM is embedded here (ERi − rf); not a separate record.

sources.title: CAPM Beta Explained and Formula Examples (AnalystPrep blog)
sources.locator: Application of CAPM: E(Ri) = Rf + βi[E(Rm) − Rf] with worked example 5% + 1.6(10% − 5%) = 13%
sources.evidence: Page states the CAPM expected-return equation as risk-free rate plus beta times the market premium, with a worked example confirming the curated form.
sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

references.method: Source inputs in decimals: 0.025 + 1.03·0.04 = 0.0662, matching published 6.62% to stated rounding.
references.provenance: Published result: LM4 Exhibit 12, printed p. 218 (PDF p. 228)

references.method: Corroborating source's worked example: 5% + 1.6·(10% − 5%) = 13%, in decimals 0.05 + 1.6·0.05 = 0.13.
references.provenance: Published result: AnalystPrep beta/CAPM article Example 2

rejection_cases.reason: Market risk premium is required; the risk-free rate and beta alone cannot price the asset.

models.inverse_notes: rf = ERi − beta·MRP; beta = (ERi − rf)/MRP requires MRP ≠ 0; MRP = (ERi − rf)/beta requires beta ≠ 0. Cash (beta = 0) gives ERi = rf with MRP undetermined. Substitution check: ERi=0.0662, rf=0.025, MRP=0.04 recovers beta=1.03. Algebraic only.

gaps: Quantity meanings risk_free_rate, capm_beta (shared with b02), market_risk_premium, capm_expected_return are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot and require extension.
Feeds reverse-optimization imputed returns; premium-only rearrangement embedded, not duplicated.

models.title: Rebalancing corridor lower bound
models.summary: Lower edge of a tolerance band as the target weight minus the band half-width.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Portfolio Rebalancing in Practice, printed p. 279 (PDF p. 289), Example 12
relationship.translation_notes: Decimal form (unit 1). d is the one-sided band half-width in the same weight units (percentage points as decimals). Companion to the upper-bound record. Dimensional check: dimensionless − dimensionless = dimensionless weight.

variables.definition: Strategic target weight of the asset class, in decimal form
variables.context: same portfolio and rebalancing policy as L

variables.definition: One-sided tolerance band half-width around target, in decimal weight form
variables.context: same portfolio and rebalancing policy as L
variables.domain: Nonnegative; at most the target weight for a meaningful lower bound

variables.source_symbol: introduced L for lower corridor edge (e.g. 45%)
variables.definition: Lower corridor edge; drift below it triggers rebalancing review
variables.context: same portfolio and rebalancing policy as inputs
variables.domain: Weight in 0 to 1 under the stated domain

assumptions: Symmetric band around the strategic target; corridor stated as target ± tolerance.
Band widths reflect the committee's risk/transaction-cost tradeoff for that asset class.
limitations: Hitting the edge prompts review, not a mechanical trade: the source distinguishes rebalancing to target vs to corridor limits (cost vs alignment).
Optimal multi-period, multi-asset rebalancing is an unsolved problem (per source); this bounds only the single-asset corridor.

models.title: Surplus return as asset-minus-liability change per initial assets
models.summary: Surplus return equals the change in asset value minus the change in liability value, divided by initial asset value.

relationship.original_equation: Surplus return = (Change in asset value − Change in liability value) / (Initial asset value)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Surplus Optimization, printed p. 240 (PDF p. 250), surplus-return definition under Eq. 2
relationship.translation_notes: Money changes and initial assets must share one currency unit (USD label stands in for the single domestic unit; no conversion). Decimal output (unit 1). Dimensional check: (currency − currency)/currency = dimensionless.
